channel.title: Elevate · The Entertrainer Blogs
channel.description: Articles about work, learning, technology, and the questions that stay with you.

item.title: Hot tea cools. Phones die. Rest isn’t a moral failure.
item.description: Your tea didn’t fail you. It finished a sentence the universe started. Plus: why fourteen open tabs feel more respectable than a nap. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: Friend, friendly. Love, lovely. Why isn’t the Moon moonly?
item.description: A kid says the Moon has “moonly mountains” and four adults correct him. None can say why. The answer involves a clock, a lamp, and 1066. Read time: 5 minutes.

item.title: Stare at a word long enough and it stops being a word.
item.description: I stared at “door” until it stopped looking like English. That glitch has a name, an Ig Nobel Prize, and stranger cousins. Read time: 5 minutes.

item.title: Your life’s midpoint isn’t 40. One old rule says 18.
item.description: In 1877 a philosopher accused his years of getting shorter. His rule puts your life’s midpoint at 18. Here is why that number moves. Read time: 5 minutes.

item.title: You only find out you don’t know it when you explain it.
item.description: Yale volunteers rated how well they understood a zip. Then they had to explain it. The feeling of knowing is a receipt, not the item. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: The cup stays. The tea does not.
item.description: An old man watches his chai go cold on a ghat. One small word from the Chāndogya Upaniṣad names exactly that kind of looking. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: How many of you is actually inside you?
item.description: One half of a split brain saw snow and picked a shovel. The talking half never saw the snow, and calmly invented a chicken shed. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: Nobody buys the fear tone first. What all nine do
item.description: One tuning fork for fear, one for love. Guess which sells. What each of the nine sacred frequencies is said to do, and how to pick. Read time: 8 minutes.

item.title: Five lines of school algebra that prove 2 = 1
item.description: Start with a = b. Five tidy lines of school algebra later, 2 = 1. One quiet step is hiding a door that maths will not walk through. Read time: 7 minutes.
